Judgment:

1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
(herein after referred to Da vs Pawan Kumar Goel as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused have
viola
ted the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules.

2. As per the complaint, on 13.03.2002 the Food Inspector C.B. Boora purchased a sample of 'Arhar Dal" a food article for analysis from accused Pawan Kumar Goel at M/s Pawan Kumar Gaurav Kumar, Shop No. 162, Devli Road, Village Devli, New Delhi - 62, where the said food article was found stored for sale and where accused No.1 Pawan Kumar Goel was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling.

The sample consisted 750 gms of Arhar Dal Da vs Pawan Kumar Goel on 6 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78487250/
1 taken from an open gunny bag bearing no label declaration.

entities.text: Arhar Dal Da vs Pawan Kumar Goel
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The sample was taken under the supervision / direction of Sh. A.K. Singh, SDM/LHA (Kalkaji).
The sample was taken after mixing the Arhar Dal by rotating it with the help of clean and dry jhaba several times in all possible directions.
The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts by putting them in three separate clean and dry bottles.
Each bottle was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules.
The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles.
Notice was given to accused No. 1 Pawan Kumar Goel and the price of sample was also given to him vide vendor receipt dated 13.03.2002.
Panchnama too was prepared at the spot.
All the documents prepared by F.I. were signed by accused No.1 Pawan Kumar Goel and the other witness Sh Satish Kumar Gupta, FI,

Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh Satish Kumar Gupta , FI was joined as witness.
DA vs Pawan Kumar Goel 3.
One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No. AKS/LHA/001546 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition.
Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the same to be adulterated.

The report of the Public Analyst is as follows:
"The sample is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz tartarzine."
4.

It is the case of the complainant that accused No.1 Pawan Kumar Goel was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Pawan Kumar Gaurav Kumar, Shop No. 162, Devli Road, Village Devli, New Delhi - 62, at the time of sampling and as such he was incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said shop.
5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA.

The complaint was then filed in the court on 19.12.2002 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(j)&(m) and Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 of PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused.

During the trial, vide order dated 22.12.2009 accused No.
2 Mukesh Kumar Mittal was also impleaded in this case as an accused.
6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 19.12.2002.
The accused DA vs Pawan Kumar Goel thereafter exercised their option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act.

Based on the report of the CFL as well as evidence led in pre charge evidence, charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(j)&(m) of PFA Act and Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 of PFA Rules, 1955, to which accused person pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

Da vs Pawan Kumar Goel on 6 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78487250/
2 7.
At the trial, the prosecution examined four witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 SDM/LHA Sh A.K. Singh, PW-2 FI C.B. Boora, PW-3 FI Rajpal Singh, PW-4 FI Satish Kumar Gupta.

PW-2 C.B.
Boora and PW-4 FI Satish Kumar Gupta were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh. A.K. Singh.

These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample commodity of "Arhar Dal "
750 gms from the vendor for analysis, bearing no label or declaration, taking the sample of Arhar Dal and mixing help of a clean & dry jhaba, dividing the sample into three equal parts by putting them into three separate clean and dry sample bottles,
separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses.
They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C.
The accused also made statement Ex.PW1/D alongwith document Ex.PW2/A.

Thereafter, on 14.03.2002 one counterpart of the sample along with one copy of memo in form VII and another copy of memo in DA vs Pawan Kumar Goel form VII in sealed deposited with PA vide receipt Ex.PW2/B.

entities.text: DA vs Pawan Kumar Goel form VII
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The remaining two counter parts of the sample in intact condition along with two copies of memo of Form VII in a sealed packet were deposited with LHA vide LHA Receipt Ex.PW1/E under intimation that one counterpart of the same has already been deposited with PA.
Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW1/F was received, according to which the sample was adulterated because the same was coloured with synthetic colouring matter tatrazin.

Thereafter PW-2 C.B.
Boora conducted further investigation and collected reply from STO vide Ex.PW1/G.
After completion of investigation, the entire case file was put before then Director PFA for obtaining his Consent.
The then Director PFA granted his Consent for prosecution vide sanction order Ex.PW1/H.
Thereafter, the present complaint Ex.PW1/J was filed before the Court.
Then intimation letter Ex.PW1/K alongwith copy of PA Reports was sent to the accused vide postal receipt Ex.PW1/L.
These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel.
8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded wherein the accused persons denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
Thereafter matter was listed for defence evidence.
9. In their defence, the accused No. 2 Mukesh Kumar Mittal and accused No. 1 Pawan Kumar Goel examined themselves as DW-1 and DW-3.
The accused also examined one Sunil Kumar Gupta and Raghubir Saran as DW-2 and DW-4.
Thereafter defence evidence was closed vide order dated 01.07.2016 and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
DA vs Pawan Kumar Goel 10.
In a criminal case, the burden is on the prosecution to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt by leading positive evidence.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and it has to be necessary discharged by the prosecution itself.

Da vs Pawan Kumar Goel on 6 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78487250/
3 11.It is to be understood that the charge framed against the accused is for violation of section 2(ia)(a), (j) and (m) of the PFA Act read with Rules 23 and 29 of PFA Rules with respect to 'adulteration'.

Under section 2(ia)(a) of PFA Act, the prosecution has to establish that the purchaser had demanded a food article of a specific nature, substance or quality and the article sold was, to his prejudice, either not of the nature, substance or quality demanded, or was not of the nature,
substance or quality which it purported or represented to be. Section 2(ia)(j) specifically deals with colouring matter which is present other than prescribed or is present beyond the prescribed limits of variability.

Section 2(ia)
(m) of PFA Act deals with situation where the quality or purity of an article falls below the prescribed standard or its constituents are present in quantities not within the prescribed limits of variability.
12. The commodity in the present case is Dal Arhar which is food grain and has to be tested as per the standards prescribed for food grains.
It is clear that this article falls in Item A.18.06.09 of Appendix B to the PFA Rules.
Both the analysts have applied the same standards to this product.
It is nowhere the stand of the accused that the food article does not fall under this head or that it falls under some other head.
DA vs Pawan Kumar Goel 13.
It is pertinent to note that both the chemical experts, PA and CFL, have found the presence of the synthetic colouring matter Tartrazine which is a totally prohibited item in the sample analysed.
On this point, both the reports are in conformity to each other and not at variance.

14. The defence taken by the accused No. 1, the vendor is that he had purchased this dal from M/s Shyam Lal Raj Kumar of Naya Bazar through broker Sh. Sunil Kumar Gupta and has paid for this dal by cheque.
According to accused No. 1 he had purchased the dal vide bill Ex.DA.
However the defence of accused No. 2 is that the dal in question does not belong to him, it might have been purchased by accused No. 1 from somewhere else.
He has further denied bill Ex.DA during his evidence as DW-1.
The accused No. 1 has placed on record the bill Ex.DA in his evidence.

The accused No. 1 has also put this question to PW-1 and PW-2 the Food Inspector, they both deposed that accused No. 1 had not informed that he had purchased the dal ahrar from M/s Shyam Lal Raj Kumar Naya Bazar Delhi vide bill No. 50183 dated 04.03.2002.
15.

entities.text: Shyam Lal Raj Kumar Naya Bazar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that no such bill/invoice/cash memo of purchase of this Dal had been shown to the FI or the name of the supplier disclosed to him at the time of sampling.

Even if his stand is accepted that the FI had refused to accept the bill at the spot (though there is no evidence to this effect, except bald suggestions that were denied by the PWs), still nothing had prevented him from sending the documents to the PFA department DA vs Pawan Kumar Goel at any time thereafter at the first available opportunity or even during the course of investigation.

No such stand was taken or name of the supplier disclosed even in letter Ex.PW-1/D given by the accused No.1 to the FI, so as to enable the FI to investigate the role of the supplier and to implicate or exonerate it.

When the complainant was not even informed about the particulars of the supplier, the accused Da vs Pawan Kumar Goel on 6 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78487250/
4 cannot say that the FI did not verify the facts.
16. Be that as it may, it would be no defence available to the accused to claim that he was not the manufacturer of the commodity in question or that he was only a retailer using the same.
A seller or packer or distributor or manufacturer would operate in different fields and all of them can be held liable in their separate areas.
Sale of adulterated food article is prohibited.

The definition of 'sale'
under section 2 (xiii) is very wide which includes storing or exposing for sale as a retailer and even attempt to sell and also sale for analysis.

The only benefit which the accused can claim on this ground is under section 19(2) of PFA Act which would apply only if he is able to show that he had purchased the product against a warranty and had been selling the product in the same manner as purchased by him.
17. Even if the documents relied upon by him are accepted, that would not come to his rescue.
There is nothing to connect the lifted sample of dal arhar to the dal allegedly purchased through these documents bill Ex.DA.
The dal was lifted from an open gunny bag bearing no label declaration.

Thus, there is nothing to show that the dal lifted from the shop, was the same dal, which the DA vs Pawan Kumar Goel accused had allegedly purchased from DW-1 vide bill Ex.DA placed on record by him or any particular bill amongst these bills.
18. Even otherwise, the bill produced by the accused do not qualify to give warranty to the accused under section 19(2) of the PFA Act.
For that, specific language is to be used as per Rule 12-A and as per Form-VIA, PFA Rules.
Reliance in this regard can be placed on M/s.

Muralidhar Shyamlal v.
State of Assam [1996(I) PFA Cases 86].

entities.text:
Muralidhar Shyamlal v.
State of Assam [1996(I) PFA Cases 86]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no batch number / code number or any other means to identify the dal sold to be the one lifted.
Again, the bill/invoice should carry a warranty in the prescribed language.

Without commenting on the correctness of the language and or legality of such claim of evasion of liability under the PFA Act, it is certain that the warranty as prescribed by Rule 12-A and Form VI- A of PFA Rules is not there on the bill.

19. Further, it is to be understood that the benefit of warranty under section 19(2) of PFA Act would be available only when there is a written warranty from the supplier/seller in addition to the fact that it has been sold in the same condition as was purchased.
Both the conditions have to be fulfilled simultaneously.
There is further no evidence to the effect that the dal was in same state or condition when sold/used.
There is no witness who could depose that the dal lifted from possession of the accused was in the same condition as was purchased though the bill in question.
Thus, even the benefit of warranty cannot be extended to the accused in this case.

20. The case in hand would be therefore covered under section 2(ia) DA vs Pawan Kumar Goel (a) of PFA Act as there is evidence to show that it was not of the nature, substance or quality which it is purported to be as per PFA Rules.
The case would fall under section 2(ia)(j) as there is presence of colour which is not permitted in this article.
Violation of section 2(ia)(j) is punishable under section 16(1A) and violation of section 2(ia)(a) is punishable under section 16(i)(a) of PFA Act.
But being graver offence, conviction can be under section 16(1A) of PFA Act.

Da vs Pawan Kumar Goel on 6 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78487250/
5 21.
Having said so, it can be said that the complainant / prosecution has been able to establish its case and prove the guilt of the accused No. 1 beyond the shadow of reasonable doubt.

It has been proved that the accused no. 1 had sold adulterated food in violation of section 2(ia)(a) and (j) of PFA Act read with Rules 23, 28 and 29 of PFA Rules, and has committed the offence punishable under section 7/16(1A) of PFA Act.
22.
Thus, the accused No. 1 is held guilty and convicted for the offence punishable under section 16(1A) of the PFA Act.
The accused No. 2 is acquitted.
Let the matter be listed for arguments on sentence on behalf of accused No.1.
